structured_output.steelman: A learner holding a current-term and a next-term instalment should be able to tick the invoices they want to settle, see the summed total change as they tick, and go through one checkout for exactly that set — so nobody is forced into all-or-nothing or into two separate payments. The card and checkout already exist; this adds a selection state and carries it into checkout.

ambiguities.text: Whether the external invoicing/payments provider accepts one payment against a named set of invoices, or only a single amount. AC3 ("checkout for exactly the checked invoices") and AC4 ("mark the paid invoices as paid and leave the others open") require per-invoice allocation; the spec's dependency ("the checkout page accepts an amount") does not establish it. If the provider takes only an amount, Finance must also state the allocation rule for a single payment across open invoices.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Engineer builds the selection state, reaches checkout, finds the provider settles one invoice per transaction or one amount with no allocation — then either ships a total that marks nothing paid, or invents an allocation rule on Finance's ledger.

ambiguities.text: Whether a learner may pay a later instalment while an earlier (possibly overdue) one stays open. The outcome says "the ones they choose", implying any subset; Finance has not said so explicitly.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: If Finance requires earliest-first, the checkboxes are ordered, not independent, and AC1/AC2 change shape after the card is built.

ambiguities.text: How wallet tuition credit (referral credit) applies to the "Pay selected" total — netted before display, and against which selected invoice first.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: AC2's "sum of the checked invoices" and the amount sent to checkout differ once credit exists; the engineer has to pick whether the card shows gross or net.

ambiguities.text: How the selection reaches checkout when the checkout page today accepts an amount, not invoice IDs; and what checkout shows for a multi-invoice payment.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The 'checkout link that carries the selection' in the Size line is the real work; if checkout must be extended to accept invoice IDs, that is a second surface, not a link.

ambiguities.text: Card state between checkout success and the paid mark (up to 60 seconds): pending indicator, and whether a learner can start a second payment for the same invoices in that window.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Without a pending state a learner can double-pay in the gap, and the Figma may not cover it.

ambiguities.text: Behaviour when a payment for a set partly succeeds (provider settles some invoices, rejects others).
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: AC4 only covers full success; the engineer has to decide what 'paid' means on the card for a half-settled set.

hidden_dependencies.name: External invoicing/payments provider — multi-invoice payment and allocation
hidden_dependencies.why: The spec names the myNXU checkout page but not the provider behind it. Platform context states it is unknown whether the provider supports paying a subset of open invoices. Every AC after the first depends on this; the spec cannot be sized without the answer.

hidden_dependencies.name: Wallet tuition credit (referral programme, set by Finance)
hidden_dependencies.why: Credits sit in the same wallet the card reads from. The spec's total ignores them; the existing single-invoice flow presumably nets them. Which invoice credit is applied to first is a Finance rule.

hidden_dependencies.name: Deadline rail — invoice issued/paid events
hidden_dependencies.why: AC4's 60-second paid mark rides on the existing invoice-paid event. With a set, the rail must clear only the paid invoices' items; if the provider emits one event per payment rather than per invoice, the rail needs mapping work.

size.risk: Provider capability. If the provider accepts a payment against named invoice IDs and checkout can pass them, this is S as stated. If the provider takes one amount only, the team builds allocation and reconciliation on top of the payment, plus a checkout change — that is L and carries a Finance ledger rule the team does not own.

refinement_agenda: With Finance's provider answer in hand: choose the checkout mechanism — invoice IDs passed through to the provider, or one amount with myNXU-side allocation — and re-size on that choice.
Decide how wallet credit is applied to the selected total (gross vs net on the card; allocation order across selected invoices) and fold it into AC2.
Decide the pending state between checkout success and the paid mark, and the card behaviour for a partly settled set — extend AC4 or add one AC.
structured_output.requester_message:
@finance-ops — the spec is clear and reads as a small change on the wallet card. It is held on one fact only you have.

Owed by Thursday triage:
1. Does our invoicing/payments provider accept a single payment against a chosen set of open invoices (by invoice ID)? If it only takes an amount, what is the rule for allocating one payment across open invoices — earliest due first, learner's choice, something else?
2. Confirm a learner may pay a later instalment while an earlier one is still open (the spec implies yes).
3. How wallet credit (referral credit) should apply when a learner pays a selection — netted off the total, and against which invoice first.

Once (1) is answered the team can size this in refinement with the designer and an engineer; without it the S on the spec is a guess that can become a sprint of allocation and reconciliation work.

The team is mid-sprint. If this is pulled forward, a same-sized item currently In Sprint moves out, and triage names which one on Thursday. Send the three answers before then and this goes to Ready in the same triage.
